planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start chard seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost date in April to May.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors after last frost date in May to June.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow chard seeds outdoors after last frost date in May to June.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Begin harvesting in mid to late summer and continue through early fall.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start chard seeds indoors 4-6 weeks before last frost date in March to April.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors after last frost date in May to June.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow chard seeds outdoors in spring in April to May.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Begin harvesting in early summer and continue through fall.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start chard seeds indoors in early spring and again in mid-summer for fall harvest.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors in spring and fall.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow chard seeds in early spring and mid to late summer.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest in late spring and again in fall and early winter.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start chard seeds indoors in early fall in September to October.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors in late fall in November to December.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow chard seeds in fall and early winter.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest during mild winter months from December through March.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start chard seeds indoors in fall and early winter.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant seedlings outdoors in winter months.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow chard seeds in fall and winter.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Harvest during cool season months in winter and early spring.

varieties.name: Bright Lights
varieties.description: Bright Lights is a stunning multi-colored chard variety that brings vibrant ornamental appeal to vegetable gardens. This hybrid produces large, crinkled leaves in shades of green, yellow, orange, red, pink, and purple, with matching colorful stems. Despite its beauty, it's highly productive and has excellent flavor with tender leaves and mild taste.

appearance.leaf_color: Multi-colored (green, red, pink, orange, yellow, purple)

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4-6 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, tender, slightly sweet with subtle earthy undertones

leafCropCharacteristics.head_type: Loose leaves on thick colorful stems

varieties.fun_fact: Bright Lights chard was an All-America Selections winner in 1995 and is one of the most visually stunning vegetables you can grow, making it popular in ornamental potagers and cottage gardens.
varieties.planting_tip: Bright Lights thrives in full sun where the leaf colors are most vibrant, though it tolerates partial shade. Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep in spring or transplant seedlings. Space plants 6-12 inches apart depending on desired leaf size. Keep soil consistently moist for tender leaves. Begin harvesting outer leaves when they're 4-6 inches long by cutting at the base. Regular harvesting encourages continuous production. This variety is stunning in containers and mixed vegetable beds. Leaves are beautiful in raw salads and retain their colors somewhat when cooked.

varieties.name: Fordhook Giant
varieties.description: Fordhook Giant is a classic heirloom chard variety with large, dark green savoyed leaves and thick, white, tender stems. This vigorous grower produces abundant, high-quality harvests and is one of the most dependable chard varieties for home gardeners. The substantial stems are especially prized for cooking and have a mild, slightly sweet flavor.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate to heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, tender, slightly sweet with subtle mineral notes

leafCropCharacteristics.head_type: Loose leaves on thick white stems

varieties.fun_fact: Fordhook Giant has been a favorite since the 1930s and remains one of the best-performing chard varieties for long harvests and reliability in both home and commercial gardens.
varieties.planting_tip: Fordhook Giant is extremely productive and reliable, making it perfect for succession plantings. Direct sow seeds or transplant seedlings in spring or summer. Space plants 9-12 inches apart to allow room for large leaves and thick stems. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged. Harvest by cutting outer leaves at the base or by removing the entire leaf stem. The thick white stems are tender and delicious when separated from leaves and sautéed. This variety continues producing until frost and can provide 3-4 months of continuous harvest.

varieties.name: Lucullus
varieties.description: Lucullus is a heirloom Swiss chard variety with crinkled, yellow-green leaves and pale yellow stems. This cold-hardy, productive variety has tender leaves and mild flavor that's excellent for cooking. It's been cultivated since the 1800s and is popular in European cuisine for both leaves and stems.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4-6 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, tender, delicate with subtle sweetness

leafCropCharacteristics.head_type: Loose leaves on pale yellow stems

varieties.fun_fact: Lucullus chard is named after Lucullus, a wealthy Roman general famous for his lavish feasts, reflecting the culinary elegance this vegetable brings to European cooking traditions.
varieties.planting_tip: Lucullus is an excellent choice for spring and fall gardening and performs well in both seasons. Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep or transplant seedlings. Space plants 9-12 inches apart. The distinctive yellow-green leaves make it visually interesting in the garden and on the plate. Keep soil consistently moist and apply mulch to help regulate temperature and moisture. Begin harvesting when leaves are 6-8 inches long by cutting outer stems at the base. The pale yellow stems are particularly tender and cook quickly. This variety is excellent for succession planting for continuous harvest.

varieties.name: Ruby Red
varieties.description: Ruby Red is a stunning chard variety with deep crimson-red stems and dark green leaves with prominent red veining. This colorful variety is both ornamental and productive, offering excellent flavor with slightly earthy, sweet notes. The vibrant red stems retain their color when cooked and add visual drama to any dish or garden bed.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4-6 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Earthy, slightly sweet with subtle mineral notes and mild flavor

leafCropCharacteristics.head_type: Loose leaves on thick red stems
leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth to slightly crinkled, tender, large

varieties.fun_fact: Ruby Red chard's vibrant color comes from betalain pigments, the same compounds found in beets! These antioxidants are believed to have anti-inflammatory properties.
varieties.planting_tip: Ruby Red chard performs best in full sun where the red coloring is most intense. Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep in spring or summer, spacing 8-12 inches apart. The dramatic coloring makes this variety excellent for ornamental edible gardens and containers. Keep soil consistently moist for the most tender leaves. Harvest outer leaves when 6-8 inches long, cutting at the base of the stem. The red stems are beautiful when separated from leaves and sautéed separately. Young leaves can be used raw in salads for a colorful addition.

varieties.name: Peppermint
varieties.description: Peppermint is a striking chard variety featuring candy-cane striped stems in bright pink and white with dark green leaves and pink veining. This eye-catching variety combines ornamental beauty with excellent culinary quality. The stems are tender and sweet, and the overall plant adds a whimsical, colorful element to gardens and dishes alike.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4-6 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, sweet, tender with delicate flavor

leafCropCharacteristics.head_type: Loose leaves on pink and white striped stems
leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth to slightly savoyed, tender, medium to large

varieties.fun_fact: Peppermint chard's striped stems look so much like candy canes that it's often planted in children's gardens to make vegetables more appealing and fun to grow and eat!
varieties.planting_tip: Peppermint chard is as easy to grow as it is beautiful. Direct sow seeds in spring through summer, spacing 8-12 inches apart. This variety thrives in full sun where stem colors are most vibrant. The candy-striped appearance makes it perfect for ornamental containers and edible landscaping. Keep soil consistently moist and harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage continued production. The striking stems are beautiful when displayed whole in cooking. Young leaves work well in raw salads, while mature leaves are excellent sautéed.

varieties.name: Perpetual Spinach
varieties.description: Perpetual Spinach, also called spinach beet or leaf beet, is a chard variety that closely resembles spinach in both appearance and flavor. This variety produces smooth, tender leaves with narrow stems and a mild, spinach-like taste. It's more heat-tolerant than true spinach and provides continuous harvests throughout the growing season, making it an excellent spinach alternative for summer gardens.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4-6 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, spinach-like, tender with subtle sweetness

varieties.fun_fact: Perpetual Spinach is actually a type of chard (Beta vulgaris) rather than true spinach (Spinacia oleracea), but it fooled gardeners for centuries with its spinach-like leaves and flavor!
varieties.planting_tip: Perpetual Spinach is the solution for gardeners who love spinach but struggle with bolting in warm weather. Direct sow seeds in spring through summer, spacing 6-10 inches apart. This variety thrives in full sun to partial shade and tolerates heat much better than true spinach. Keep soil consistently moist for the most tender, mild-flavored leaves. Begin harvesting outer leaves when 4-6 inches long. Young leaves are excellent raw in salads, while larger leaves work well cooked like spinach. This variety can produce continuously for months with regular harvesting.

varieties.name: Rhubarb Chard
varieties.description: Rhubarb Chard is a beautiful heirloom variety featuring deep red to burgundy stems and dark green, glossy leaves with red veining. This variety resembles rhubarb in appearance and offers rich, earthy flavor with slightly sweet undertones. It's both ornamental and highly productive, making it a favorite for gardens where beauty and function matter equally.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate to heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, earthy, slightly sweet with deeper flavor than green varieties

leafCropCharacteristics.head_type: Loose leaves on thick burgundy-red stems
leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth to slightly crinkled, tender, large

varieties.fun_fact: Despite its name and appearance, Rhubarb Chard is not related to rhubarb at all! The name comes from the stunning red stems that resemble rhubarb stalks, though chard stems are much more tender.
varieties.planting_tip: Rhubarb Chard is a vigorous grower that performs well in full sun where the red color intensifies. Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep or transplant seedlings, spacing 9-12 inches apart. This heirloom variety is excellent in ornamental borders and edible landscapes. Keep soil consistently moist and provide regular feeding for the best production. Harvest outer leaves when 6-8 inches long. The dramatic red stems are stunning when cooked and hold their color better than some red varieties. This variety continues producing well into fall and can withstand light frosts.

varieties.name: Golden Sunrise
varieties.description: Golden Sunrise is a cheerful chard variety with bright golden-yellow stems and medium green leaves with yellow veining. This variety brings sunshine to the garden with its vibrant coloring while offering tender, mild-flavored leaves and sweet stems. It's less common than red or white varieties but equally productive and visually striking.

care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeder, apply balanced fertilizer every 4-6 weeks

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, sweet, tender with delicate, pleasant flavor

leafCropCharacteristics.head_type: Loose leaves on bright yellow stems
leafCropCharacteristics.leaf_texture: Smooth to slightly crinkled, tender, medium to large

varieties.fun_fact: Golden Sunrise chard's bright yellow stems are particularly high in beta-carotene and bring a cheerful, sunny appearance to both gardens and plates—perfect for brightening up dreary days!
varieties.planting_tip: Golden Sunrise thrives in full sun where the golden color is most vibrant. Direct sow seeds in spring or summer, spacing 8-12 inches apart. The bright yellow stems make this variety excellent for colorful mixed plantings and containers. Keep soil consistently moist and well-fed for tender, sweet-tasting stems. Harvest outer leaves when 6-8 inches long by cutting at the base. The golden stems are particularly sweet and tender, making them delicious when sautéed separately from the leaves. This variety pairs beautifully with red-stemmed varieties for a colorful display.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start asparagus seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost in February to March for crown production.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant crowns or seedlings outdoors after last frost in May to June into prepared beds.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow asparagus seeds in spring in April to May, though crown planting is preferred.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Do not harvest the first two years. Begin light harvest in year 3, increasing to full harvest by year 4.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start asparagus seeds indoors in late winter in February to March.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant crowns or seedlings outdoors in spring in April to May.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow asparagus seeds in spring in April to May.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Begin light harvest in year 3, increasing to full harvest by year 4. Harvest spears until early summer.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start asparagus seeds indoors in January to February.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant crowns or seedlings outdoors in early spring in March to April.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow asparagus seeds in early spring in March to April.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Begin light harvest in year 3. Harvest spears in spring before heat stress begins.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start asparagus seeds indoors in fall in October to November.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant crowns or seedlings outdoors in late fall in December to January.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow asparagus seeds in late fall in November to December.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Begin light harvest in year 3 during cool season months.

planting_dates_description.start_indoors: Start asparagus seeds indoors in early fall in September to October.
planting_dates_description.transplant: Transplant crowns or seedlings outdoors in late fall in November to December.
planting_dates_description.start_outdoors: Direct sow asparagus seeds in fall in October to November.
planting_dates_description.harvest: Begin light harvest in year 3 during winter months. Provide afternoon shade in summer.

varieties.name: Jersey Knight
varieties.description: Jersey Knight is a modern all-male hybrid asparagus variety renowned for its exceptional productivity and vigor. As an all-male cultivar, it doesn't waste energy producing seeds, resulting in thicker, more abundant spears. This variety produces consistently high yields of thick, uniform, dark green spears and has excellent disease resistance.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week during growing season
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1-2 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Tender, mild, slightly sweet with delicate grassy undertones

varieties.fun_fact: Jersey Knight was developed at Rutgers University in New Jersey and is an all-male hybrid, meaning it produces 30-40% more spears than traditional varieties because it doesn't produce seeds.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Jersey Knight crowns in early spring in well-prepared beds amended with lots of organic matter. Dig trenches 6-8 inches deep and space crowns 12-18 inches apart. Cover crowns with 2 inches of soil initially, then gradually fill in the trench as shoots emerge. Do not harvest any spears the first two years to allow the crown to establish. In year 3, harvest lightly for 4-6 weeks. By year 4 and beyond, harvest for 8-10 weeks until spears become thin. Mulch heavily to suppress weeds and maintain moisture. Cut ferns back in fall after they yellow.

varieties.name: Mary Washington
varieties.description: Mary Washington is a classic heirloom asparagus variety developed in the early 1900s by the USDA and named after George Washington's home in Virginia. This open-pollinated variety produces tall plants with attractive fern-like foliage and dependable yields of flavorful spears. While not all-male, it has excellent vigor and disease resistance.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week during growing season
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 0.75-1.5 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, tender, delicate with pleasant asparagus flavor

varieties.fun_fact: Mary Washington asparagus was a gift from George Washington's home Mount Vernon to the USDA and has been one of America's most beloved heirloom varieties for over a century.
varieties.planting_tip: Mary Washington thrives in full sun with well-draining soil enriched with compost or aged manure. Plant crowns in early spring 6-8 inches deep, spacing them 12-18 inches apart. Fill in trenches gradually as shoots emerge. This variety produces seed, which means some plant energy is directed to seed production rather than new spears, so yields are slightly lower than all-male varieties. However, it's a reliable, long-lived variety that can produce for 20+ years with proper care. Let the ferns grow tall in summer—they feed the crown. Cut them down in fall after frost.

varieties.name: Purple Passion
varieties.description: Purple Passion is a unique, visually striking asparagus variety with deep purple spears that turn green when cooked. This Italian heirloom produces tender, sweet spears and is prized by gourmet chefs for its distinctive appearance and subtle flavor differences. The purple color indicates high anthocyanin content with potential health benefits.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week during growing season
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1-1.5 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, tender, slightly more delicate than green varieties with subtle nuttiness

varieties.fun_fact: Purple Passion asparagus contains higher levels of anthocyanins, the same antioxidant compounds found in blueberries and red wine, making it not only beautiful but potentially more nutritious.
varieties.planting_tip: Purple Passion requires the same cultural practices as other asparagus varieties but is somewhat less cold hardy than green varieties, making it better suited to zones 6 and warmer. Plant crowns in well-prepared beds with excellent drainage in early spring. Space 12-18 inches apart and plant 6-8 inches deep. The distinctive purple color is most vibrant in cool weather and fades slightly in hot summers. Do not harvest the first two years. Beginning in year 3, harvest spears when they're 6-8 inches tall for best tenderness. The purple color turns green when steamed or boiled, but grilling preserves some of the purple hue. This variety makes an excellent ornamental as well as productive plant.

varieties.name: Jersey Giant
varieties.description: Jersey Giant is an all-male hybrid asparagus variety developed at Rutgers University, known for producing exceptionally large, thick spears with excellent flavor. This vigorous variety is highly productive and disease-resistant, yielding uniform, dark green spears that are tender and flavorful. Jersey Giant is one of the most reliable commercial and home garden varieties available.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week during growing season
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1.5-2.5 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Tender, sweet, mild with excellent classic asparagus flavor

rootCharacteristics.texture: Robust fibrous roots with strong crowns

varieties.fun_fact: Jersey Giant produces spears so thick and uniform that it's a favorite among commercial growers—some spears can be as thick as a quarter! It's part of the famous 'Jersey' series developed at Rutgers University.
varieties.planting_tip: Jersey Giant thrives in full sun with deep, well-draining soil rich in organic matter. Plant crowns in early spring in trenches 8-10 inches deep, spacing 12-18 inches apart. Cover initially with 2-3 inches of soil and gradually fill as shoots emerge. This variety's vigor means it can produce harvestable spears slightly earlier than other varieties—lightly harvest in year 3 for 3-4 weeks, then extend to 8-10 weeks from year 4 onward. Apply heavy mulch and feed generously after harvest season. The thick spears are best harvested when 6-8 inches tall for optimal tenderness.

varieties.name: Millennium
varieties.description: Millennium is a modern all-male hybrid asparagus variety bred for exceptional cold hardiness and disease resistance. This variety produces high yields of medium to large, dark green spears with excellent flavor and tenderness. Millennium performs exceptionally well in northern climates and has superior tolerance to asparagus diseases, making it one of the most reliable varieties for challenging growing conditions.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week during growing season
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1.25-2 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, tender, mild with pleasant classic flavor

varieties.fun_fact: Millennium asparagus was specifically bred to thrive in the coldest asparagus-growing regions and is one of the few varieties that performs reliably in zone 3, making it a game-changer for northern gardeners!
varieties.planting_tip: Millennium is ideal for cold-climate gardeners in zones 3-8. Plant crowns in early spring as soon as soil can be worked, in trenches 6-8 inches deep with 12-18 inches spacing. This variety's exceptional cold hardiness means it breaks dormancy reliably even after harsh winters. Plant in full sun with well-amended soil for best results. The superior disease resistance makes Millennium particularly valuable in areas with asparagus disease pressure. Do not harvest for the first two years, then harvest lightly in year 3. Mulch heavily in fall to protect crowns in coldest climates.

varieties.name: UC 157
varieties.description: UC 157 is a heat-tolerant asparagus variety developed by the University of California specifically for warmer climates. This all-male hybrid produces consistent yields of medium-sized, green spears with excellent flavor even in regions where traditional varieties struggle. UC 157 has good disease resistance and performs reliably in mild-winter, hot-summer climates.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1.5-2 inches per week, especially in hot weather
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1-1.75 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Mild, tender, pleasant with good flavor even in warm conditions

rootCharacteristics.root_size: Well-adapted crown system for warm climates

varieties.fun_fact: UC 157 is one of the few asparagus varieties that can produce reliably in California's Central Valley and other hot-summer regions where traditional cold-loving varieties fail to thrive!
varieties.planting_tip: UC 157 is specifically suited for zones 7-10 and warm-climate regions with mild winters. Plant crowns in late winter or early spring in well-draining soil amended with organic matter. Space 12-18 inches apart in trenches 6-8 inches deep. This variety requires less winter chill than traditional varieties, making it ideal for Mediterranean and warm climates. Provide consistent moisture during hot weather and mulch heavily to keep roots cool. In very hot climates, afternoon shade can be beneficial. Harvest spears when 6-8 inches tall before tips begin to open.

varieties.name: Precoce d'Argenteuil
varieties.description: Precoce d'Argenteuil is a treasured French heirloom asparagus variety dating back to the 1800s, renowned for producing thick, white spears with purple-tinged tips when grown using traditional blanching methods. This variety has exceptional flavor and is prized in European cuisine for its tender, sweet spears. It can be grown as green or white asparagus depending on cultivation method.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week during growing season
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1-1.5 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Exceptionally sweet, tender, delicate with refined flavor and minimal bitterness

varieties.fun_fact: Precoce d'Argenteuil is the traditional variety used for producing white asparagus in France and Germany! The spears are mounded with soil to blanch them, creating the pale, tender spears prized in European haute cuisine.
varieties.planting_tip: Precoce d'Argenteuil can be grown as green asparagus using standard methods or as white asparagus using traditional blanching. For green asparagus, plant crowns 6-8 inches deep in early spring with 14-20 inches spacing. For white asparagus production, mound 8-12 inches of soil over the planting area in spring and harvest spears when they just begin to emerge from the mound. This labor-intensive method produces the prized white spears. This variety performs best in zones 4-8 with cold winters. The thick spears and exceptional flavor make the extra effort worthwhile for gourmet gardeners.

varieties.name: Atlas
varieties.description: Atlas is a robust all-male hybrid asparagus variety developed for exceptional productivity and uniformity. This variety produces abundant, thick, dark green spears with tight tips and excellent flavor. Atlas has strong disease resistance and vigorous growth, making it a reliable choice for both commercial production and home gardens seeking maximum yields.

care_requirements.water_requirement: Regular watering, 1-2 inches per week during growing season
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder, apply balanced fertilizer in spring and after harvest

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1.5-2.5 pounds per plant annually after year 3

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, tender, classic asparagus flavor with excellent quality

rootCharacteristics.texture: Very robust fibrous roots with strong crowns

varieties.fun_fact: Atlas asparagus is named for the Greek Titan who held up the sky, reflecting this variety's exceptional strength, vigor, and ability to support heavy yields year after year!
varieties.planting_tip: Atlas performs best in full sun with deep, fertile, well-draining soil rich in organic matter. Plant crowns in early spring in trenches 8-10 inches deep, spacing 12-18 inches apart. This variety's exceptional vigor means it establishes quickly and can begin light harvesting in year 3. From year 4 onward, harvest for 8-10 weeks, cutting spears when 6-8 inches tall. The thick, uniform spears make Atlas excellent for freezing and commercial production. Apply heavy mulch and fertilize generously in spring and after harvest season. Cut back ferns in fall after they turn yellow. Atlas is suitable for zones 3-8.
